name: Double Takes
description: Double Takes is a western domino game played with a double-15 set, using the larger value range to support long sessions and more complex end control. Players use standard matching placements while managing high-value risk and mobility across a wide range of open-end values.

overview.description: Double Takes is a western domino game played with a double-15 set, using the larger value range to support long sessions and more complex end control. Players use standard matching placements while managing high-value risk and mobility across a wide range of open-end values.

history.origins: Double Takes is encountered as a modern large-set domino format that relies on extended western domino sets for longer and less blocked sessions.
timeline: Modern era: extended domino sets become widely used for specialized formats.
history.cultural: Played socially as a longer session game where careful mobility planning is rewarded.
history.evolution: The larger value range increases complexity in end control and blocking, and makes high-number tiles more consequential.

setup.dealing: Deal tiles by player count; remaining tiles form a boneyard if the profile uses draws.
setup.equipment: Domino set and optional score tracking by match profile.

rules.objective: Play legal matching tiles and end hands with the best score under the match profile.
rules.gameplay: Players place a legal tile to a matching open end of the shared layout. When blocked, the match profile determines whether to draw from a boneyard or pass. Hands end when a player empties their hand or play is blocked, and scoring follows the match profile in use.
keyRules: A played tile must match the value of an exposed open end.
Blocked turns are resolved by draw-or-pass profile rules.
Hand-end and scoring depend on the match profile.

strategy.basic: Keep connectors that cover multiple values and avoid holding high-number tiles too long.
strategy.intermediate: Track which high values have appeared so you do not open values you cannot reliably answer.
strategy.advanced: Shape open ends to pressure opponents into awkward values while keeping safe exits across the broad range.
tips: High-number tiles are leverage and liability; expose them only with backup.
Preserve mid-range flexibility to avoid being forced into a single dangerous value.

synthesis.shortDescription: Double Takes is a double-15 domino connecting game where the wide value range increases end-control complexity and risk.
